item.content:encoded:
3 years studying trading, almost no live trading. Blew a demo account. What would you do?

Open thread • Replies: 10 • Updated: 2026-11-19 23:47 UTC

OP

I've been learning trading for about 3 years, but I haven't been trading for 3 years. Most of that time was studying, watching videos, and building tools. I've never put real money on the line, and I want to be honest about that.

What went wrong: I built a bot that copies signals from a Telegram group straight into MetaTrader 5, using an AI to read the messages. On a demo account it looked great at first (+235 EUR in the first week). Then I scaled it up to 10 lots and in a single day it lost over 1,000 EUR. One stop loss was roughly 25% of the account. The signals weren't the problem, my position sizing was. I burned the account on paper, but it was a lesson I needed before touching real money.

Since then I've also:
- Backtested an intraday EA on an index: it lost money across years, worst streak 12 losses in a row. Dropped it.
- Run a genetic robot generator on gold: the best results looked great until I noticed the average loss per trade was ~1,860 USD when the planned risk was 200. The lot calculation was wrong, and I had also peeked at the test period, so it doesn't count as a clean test.

Where I am now: I stopped copying signals. I'm studying one model (liquidity sweeps, structure breaks, fair value gaps) on one instrument, NASDAQ, in one time window. The plan is 100 backtested trades in replay, then 30 on demo with fixed risk (0.5% per trade, max 2 losses a day), and only then a prop firm evaluation. Zero real money until then.

Questions:
1. If you've blown an account, what actually fixed it? Rules, journaling, smaller size, taking a break?
2. Is my plan sensible, or am I overcomplicating things? Should I just trade tiny size live earlier?
3. How long did it take you to become consistent, and what was the real turning point?

I'm not looking for signals, groups, or anyone's course. Just honest experiences. Thanks for reading.
